content.title: Development: Neighborhood Meetings
content.summary: The City of Arvada requires neighborhood meetings to engage local residents, property owners, and homeowners associations in the development review process before formal applications are submitted. These meetings, which are typically held on Wednesday or Thursday evenings, allow applicants to present their projects and address community concerns, while the assigned City Planner provides guidance on the process. Applicants must schedule the meetings in coordination with their City Planner and ensure proper notice is sent to nearby property owners at least 15 days prior to the meeting.
content.body:
The City of Arvada promotes citizen participation throughout the development review process through multiple avenues, including neighborhood meetings. Neighborhood meetings are held to inform neighboring property owners, homeowners associations (HOAs), and neighborhood groups of the details of a concept development before specific types of applications can be submitted to the City. These meetings are forums where the Applicant and community members should strive to work together in good faith.

## Overview

Neighborhood meetings are required prior to a formal application being submitted for development applications that require a public hearing before the Planning Commission or City Council.

The Community and Economic Development Director can also require a neighborhood meeting prior to other types of applications at their discretion.

Meetings must be scheduled in coordination with your assigned City Planner and must generally be held on Wednesday or Thursday evenings starting around 6 PM.

The applicant is responsible for hosting and running the neighborhood meeting as well as describing the development, potential impacts on the community, and answering questions about the development. The assigned City Planner will be present to answer questions about the process and other opportunities for public participation.

This information intended to assist in the preparation of scheduling and hosting the neighborhood meeting. Every applicant should also review Land Development Code (LDC) [§8-2-3-4, Neighborhood Meetings](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=COARCO_CH8DEREPR_ART8-2GEREPR_DIV8-2-3STDEKIPR_8-2-3-4NEME), and [Division 8-2-4, Required Notices](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=COARCO_CH8DEREPR_ART8-2GEREPR_DIV8-2-4RENO), to be familiar with the meeting and noticing requirements.

## Scheduling

To ensure that community members have the greatest possibility to participate, neighborhood meetings cannot be held on the same day as other public meetings or other neighborhood meetings. Monday evenings are reserved for City Council meetings and Tuesday evenings are typically reserved for Planning Commission meetings. The preferred days of the week for meetings are Wednesday and Thursday evenings.

Contact the City Planner that was assigned to your project at your pre-application meeting at least 3 weeks prior to your preferred neighborhood meeting date. The Planner will review the current meeting schedule and provide you with suggested dates.

If holding an in-person meeting, the applicant will need to locate and reserve a venue for the meeting. The meeting location should be within approximately 1.5 miles of the project location. A recommended list of locations is provided at the end of this page. Work with your Planner to ensure the venue location and size is appropriate.

If holding a virtual meeting, the applicant will need to choose a virtual meeting platform and ensure they have the capability to host a meeting.

## Notice

Once a date, time, and location have been approved by the Planner, they will provide a notice template for the applicant to complete. The notice includes contact details for the applicant and Planner, details of the meeting, a summary of the project, a summary of the process, and a vicinity map.

The summary of the project should be a 3-5 sentence statement that accurately and transparently describes the project and any potential items of community interest.

Once the template is completed, the Planner will review and approve it to be mailed. The applicant is responsible for printing and mailing the notice. Notice should be sent by standard mail and must be postmarked at least 15 calendar days before the meeting date.

**Mailed notices must be sent to:**

- All property owners within 1,000 feet of the project site (for sites under 5 acres) or 1,500 feet (for properties 5 acres or larger). Property owner addresses can be found using [Jefferson County](https://gis.jeffco.us/webmaps/jmap/index.html) and [Adams County](https://gisapp.adcogov.org/Html5Viewer/index.html?viewer=BasicMobile.BasicMobile) GIS applications.
- [Registered neighborhood groups](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=b81024c598674ff2bdae3a6f14e95723) that have boundaries within one-half mile of the project site (electronically)
- HOAs in the vicinity of the project site identified by the planner (mailed and/or electronic).
- For right-of-way or access easement vacation requests, notice shall be given to all property owners that share a boundary with the site.

The Planner will coordinate with City communications staff to have the City promote the meeting on Arvada.org, Nextdoor, and other appropriate platforms.

## Mailing Affidavit

Once notice is mailed, the applicant must complete the [Mailing Affidavit template](/DocumentCenter/View/6079/Affidavit-Certifying-Notice-of-Neighborhood-Meeting-Requirements), have it notarized, and email it to the Planner at least 10 days before the date of the meeting.

## Neighborhood Meeting

At the neighborhood meeting, City staff will be available to answer questions regarding City policies, requirements, regulations, processes, etc. but are not responsible for conducting the neighborhood meeting. The applicant is encouraged to be thoroughly prepared to answer a variety of questions from the public pertaining to the proposed development.

Preparation of the neighborhood meeting should include, at a minimum, the following:

1. A graphic presentation depicting the layout and design of the proposed development;
2. A development fact sheet including the size of the proposed project, proposed land uses, number of dwelling units, density of the project, building heights, parking requirements, land dedication, open space acreage, public recreation opportunities or facilities, etc.;
3. An explanation of  how the proposed development will be compatible with surrounding land uses and what steps the applicant has to take to ensure compatibility in the neighborhood and community; and
4. A sign-in sheet for everyone attending the meeting.

The applicant is required to provide reasonable advance notice to any qualified individual with a disability needing an accommodation. City staff can assist in identifying available resources to assist persons with visual impairments, hearing impairments, or other disabilities to fully participate in the meeting.

## After the Meeting

A summary of the neighborhood will be required to be submitted with the formal application of the project. At minimum the summary must include:

1. A notarized mailing affidavit for the dates and locations of all meetings where participants were invited to discuss the Applicant's proposal;
2. Copies of the sign-in sheets;
3. A summary of topics discussed by the Applicant and concerns, issues, and problems expressed by participants; and
4. A summary of:
   1. How the Applicant has addressed identified issues; and
   2. Issues that cannot or should not be addressed, and why those issues cannot or should not be addressed.
